newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close sharply higher, properties rebound.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close sharply higher, properties rebound.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks surged on Thursday, with the blue-chip Hang Seng Index closing above the 14,500 mark on a strong rebound by property and bank stocks, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index soared 302.60 points, or 2.13 percent, to finish at 14,506.49. Turnover increased to HK$22.05 billion from HK$17.52 billion on Wednesday.

"People seem to be getting more relaxed about properties," said Howard Gorges, a director at South China Brokerage, adding the general feeling was the post-handover government would focus on supply rather than take drastic measures against high prices.

"Property stocks had a strong rally. The banks also rallied well because obviously if (the post-handover government) doesn't take measures which knock down prices sharply in a short term then the collaterial is safer and also more likely there will be good mortgage business to be done," Gorges said.
The market's strength, which added as much as 365 points to the Hang Seng during the day, was also fuelled by heavy interest in red chips, said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
"The red chips' turnover recently accounted for about 40 percent of the market's total volume," he said.
But the market capitalisation of red chips was just about 10 percent of the total, Tang added.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations index rose 72.88 points, or 2.44 percent, to close at 3,056.86 after retreating from 3,111.23.
China Merchant jumped HK$1.40 to HK$19.15 and China Resources added HK$2.40 to HK$30.10 but Guangdong Investment eased HK$0.248 to HK$11.05.
Hang Seng Bank surged HK$4.50 to HK$96.75 on hopes that it might be among banks considered to be possible targets for acquisition by mainland companies, analysts said.
Property stocks rebounded after being oversold lately with Cheung Kong rising HK$1.50 to HK$74.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties surging HK$3.00 to HK$90.00.
June Hang Seng index futures soared 385 points to 14,560, a 53 point premium to the spot index.

But brokers said property stocks might see profit-taking pressure at high price levels since the uncertinty in the market would not go away until Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa announced the expected measures on stablising property prices.
